title: POC E2E invoke scenarios + SDK contracts sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review end-to-end invoke scenario tests, discuss SDK behavior around function/tool calling and structured output schema mismatches, and agree on next steps for validation and perf runs. Main blockers: intermittent function call schema mismatch, streaming truncation with our SDK wrapper, and flaky retry behavior under higher QPS.
action_items: Avery Chen | Share minimal repro for function-call schema mismatch + sample failing payloads | 2026-11-05
Sofia Patel | Build small instrumented test harness that runs 1k invokes with structured output verification (JSON schema) and send results | 2026-11-09
Liam O'Connor | Provide list of priority prompt families and success criteria for product acceptance | 2026-11-06
next_steps: Redwood to deliver patch for SDK streaming edge-case by Nov 8
Customer to run instrumented harness and upload CSV of failures to shared drive
Schedule 1-hour perf window (canary) next Wed Nov 10 10:00-11:00 PT to exercise high QPS scenarios
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Lead Eng, Mindpath), Priya Reddy (ML Eng, Mindpath), Jonas Meyer (Product, Mindpath)

Auto-summary: quick pulses on e2e invokes, SDK hangups, structured output failures, assign owners for repros and perf test.

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick agenda: one, run through the e2e invoke scenario results you guys uploaded; two, SDK behavior — streaming and retries; three, function-call failures and schema mismatches; and four, next steps.

[00:16] Liam: yeah thanks, uh appreciate it. We ran the 500-case harness over the weekend, sent the spreadsheet, it's in the shared drive — the sheet is called "mindpath-poc-e2e-2026-11-01.csv". Main thing: overall success ~92% but we saw a cluster of failures around the payment-tool invoke and the structured JSON output getting malformed.

[00:34] Sofia: quick question, when you say malformed — is that truncated JSON, extra commas, or mismatched types?

[00:40] Priya: a mix. Mostly truncated when streaming is enabled via the SDK wrapper. We have an internal thin wrapper that reassembles the stream and then validates against our JSON schema; about half of the stream-failure cases show a trailing comma or an unterminated object.

[00:56] Avery: okay, good detail. Sofia, did we see similar in internal runs?

[01:02] Sofia: yes, when we proxied their wrapper we could reproduce a streaming flush bug — if the client closes the connection quickly while the runtime is still flushing the last token batch, the SDK event emitter didn't always flush the final buffer, so the consumer saw an incomplete payload. That's on our SDK stream handler. We've got a patch that forces a final flush on close, but we want to test it in their harness.

[01:20] Jonas: also, separate but related: we observed some function call invocations returning unexpected extra keys which break our deserialization. For example the payment-tool returns {amount, currency} but occasionally there's a meta field called "_debug" from the model side and our parser throws.

[01:38] Sofia: hmm that sounds like schema drift from model responses — could be that the model hallucinated an auxiliary key. Two ways to handle: a) strict schema validation and drop the whole response (safer but loses some results) or b) defensive parsing that ignores unknown keys. Which is your preference?

[01:52] Liam: for product acceptance we prefer defensive parsing for now — we can't afford to lose calls. But we need to detect and log these anomalies so we can iterate on prompts.

[02:04] Priya: agreed. Also we noticed retries — when the SDK auto-retries a function call, we sometimes get duplicated side effects because the tool endpoint isn't idempotent. 

[02:16] Avery: good point. Our SDK default retry semantics are designed for transient network errors; they aren't safe for non-idempotent tool calls. The recommended pattern is to use a request-id header and make the tool idempotent or disable retries for function calls that mutate state. We should document that in the quickstart and also expose a retryPolicy per-invoke in the SDK.

[02:40] Jonas: can you show what the SDK API would look like for that?

[02:44] Sofia: sure — (paraphrase) invokeTool('payment', {amount:123}, {retryPolicy: 'no-retry', idempotencyKey: 'xyz-123'}) — something like that. We're already planning an extension to the SDK to accept call-level options.

[03:02] Liam: perfect. Back to the harness results — there were about 28 failures that matched the streaming truncation pattern and 10 that were schema extras. The rest were latency timeouts under higher concurrent load. We saw error spikes at around 80 requests per second in the test.

[03:20] Avery: that's useful. Were those runs against the hosted dev model or the dedicated pool?

[03:25] Priya: hosted dev cluster. We haven't spin up dedicated yet. We wanted to validate at the API/SDK layer first.

[03:32] Avery: makes sense. For the latency spikes we should run a controlled perf window with increased batching disabled vs enabled to see whether batching/continuous KV cache is influencing tail latencies. We'll propose a perf slot next week.

[03:48] Sofia: also a note on function calling semantics — the model sometimes emits a nested function call pattern (function A returns text that includes a suggested call to function B). Our SDK currently supports single-level function calls — we need to detect nested call suggestions and present them to the app rather than auto-executing. That will prevent runaway invocations.

[04:10] Jonas: oh yeah we saw one of those where the model suggested calling refund after a failed payment and then suggested calling notify; it got a bit recursive and our orchestration ended up attempting both. It was confusing.

[04:22] Avery: good catch. We can add a safety gate: SDK exposes a functionCallSuggestion array instead of automatically executing nested calls, and the app can decide. We'll add that to the patch.

[04:36] Liam: two practical asks from us: 1) we want the minimal repro for streaming truncation so our engs can try locally; 2) a config knob to disable streaming so we can run tests without stream reassembly to see if that alters failure rates.

[04:50] Sofia: both doable. The repro will be a small Node/py snippet that hits the SDK with a specific sequence; we can toggle stream: false in the client config.

[04:58] Priya: also request — can you add a header or metadata in logs so we can correlate call-level traces between our app and Redwood? A correlation-id.

[05:06] Avery: yes — we'll add request-id propagation and log it in the Redwood side traces. We'll share an instrumentation guide.

[05:14] Jonas: on acceptance criteria — product wants <2% structured-output validation failures for the key workflows and <200ms p50 latency for single-turn invokes in the dedicated setup. We know the hosted dev isn't representative but want those targets documented.

[05:30] Avery: noted. We'll add those to the acceptance document. For now let's focus on reducing structured-output failures to <5% in the hosted run and then revalidate on dedicated.

[05:40] Sofia: quick note about tool invocation idempotency: we can add an SDK helper that will automatically add an idempotency key and, if the tool endpoint returns a 409 duplicate, we can de-dupe. That helps non-idempotent endpoints integrate safely.

[05:56] Liam: that'll be huge. We'll also work on making payment-tool idempotent on our side but the helper buys us time.

[06:04] Priya: regarding logs and observability — we ran into an edge where the model outputs were cut off in the Firehose; the schema validator had difficulty tying the snippet back to the original prompt. Could you include the prompt hash in the stream metadata?

[06:18] Avery: yes, we can surface prompt-hash in the response envelope. We'll include it in the patch.

[06:24] Jonas: any concerns about PII with prompt-hash?

[06:28] Avery: prompt-hash is just a deterministic hash, not the content. But we will document what we log and how to opt out for regulated flows.

[06:36] Priya: security check: do you have SOC2-type docs we can hand to compliance? They asked for encryption at rest, SSO, audit logs.

[06:44] Avery: yes — we'll re-send the security pack (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, KMS options). I'll drop links into the shared drive after the call.

[06:52] Sofia: back to the structured JSON — we recommend using the SDK's post-parse hook to run a JSON schema validation step and optionally auto-correct common issues (strip unknown keys, try to repair unterminated arrays). We'll add a sample helper in the patch so you can choose the repair policy.

[07:10] Liam: can you talk through the repair heuristics? We worry about accidentally changing semantics.

[07:14] Sofia: sure — trivial repairs only: remove trailing commas, close unclosed braces if it's a single missing token, and drop unknown top-level keys. We'll never mutate numeric types or re-interpret strings. All repairs are logged with the prompt-hash.

[07:30] Jonas: sounds reasonable. If repair happens we want an audit flag to show in product UI so ops can triage high-frequency cases.

[07:36] Avery: we'll surface an incidents endpoint and spike the events into the console with counts and sample truncated payloads (redacted).

[07:46] Priya: moving on — retry semantics under load. Our harness showed duplicate side effects after SDK retry on 502s. Could you make retries opt-in per-route?

[07:56] Sofia: yes per-invoke retryPolicy and per-client default. We'll also expose a middleware to wrap function calls and apply idempotency headers automatically.

[08:06] Liam: excellent. About the perf window — we'd like Redwood to drive the canary where you route some percentage of traffic to the dedicated pool and we observe behavior. Are there capacity constraints on your side?

[08:18] Avery: our Dedicated service has reserved pools for customers, but for the POC we can spin a small dedicated buffer for the perf window. We'll want the test plan in advance: concurrency targets, sequence length distribution, and success criteria.

[08:30] Jonas: we'll share the profile. Expect 80-120 rps for short-turn workflows, a smaller number for multi-tool scenarios.

[08:40] Sofia: on instrumentation — please include sequence-length tags so we can correlate kernel selection decisions. That helps us recommend quantization/compilation profiles afterwards.

[08:50] Priya: one more oddball: in a couple of tests we saw the model attempt to call an external URL (the text included http://example...) and our tool detection flagged it as a tool call. Is there a way to distinguish plain text containing URLs vs explicit function call?

[09:04] Sofia: function calling is based on the model signal (structured function call object) not plain text, but heuristics sometimes misclassify. We'll harden the detection logic and add a threshold/guard in the SDK that requires explicit function metadata to auto-execute.

[09:20] Liam: great. Alright, recap and owners?

[09:24] Avery: recap: Sofia -> SDK patch for streaming flush, idempotency helper, per-invoke retry policy, and functionCallSuggestion array; deliver by Nov 8. Avery -> security pack and instrumentation guide by EOD Nov 4. Customer: run instrumented harness and upload results by Nov 9. We'll schedule perf canary Nov 10 10:00-11:00 PT.

[09:44] Jonas: correct. Any blockers on our side?

[09:48] Priya: none besides needing the repro and the SDK patch.

[09:52] Avery: okay we'll prioritize. Anything else?

[09:56] Liam: one ask — include a short example in the docs for nested function suggestions and recommended orchestration patterns.

[10:04] Sofia: will do. A small flowchart and example code snippet.

[10:08] Avery: perfect — we'll follow up with the artifacts in the shared drive. Thanks everyone, talk soon.

[10:16] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some minor mis-attributions and occasional filler language. References to shared artifacts: https://redwood-internal.s3/mindpath-poc/harness.csv (placeholder), security pack link placeholder: https://redwood.com/security/pack.pdf.
